title: Make the rig debug overlay panel collapsible, draggable, and resizable with correct row spacing
description:
## Summary
Rework the `RigDebugView` SceneView overlay panel chrome so it is collapsible, repositionable, and resizable, and fix the `Bone width` label overdraw by reserving an explicit row for it so every following control is pushed down. Child slice of TSK-0149; the rig drawing, focus, selection, and generic arbitrary-limb behavior are unchanged.

## User Mandate
STRICT — verbatim:

> Please make the debug rig UI toggleable/collapsable, and resizable if possible (it's okay if not). Fix the bone width text overdraw issue too by moving the rest after it down (e.g. claim that much more space if using dynamic button placement)

Binding constraints:
- The panel must collapse and expand.
- The panel must be resizable if feasible; draggable is a reasonable part of "usable chrome".
- The bone-width label must not overlap the controls after it; the controls after it must claim the label's space.

## Scope
- `Assets/Scripts/Editor/RigDebugView.cs` — overlay panel chrome and body layout.
- `Assets/Scripts/Editor/RigDebugPanelLayout.cs` (new) — pure, testable layout math (row indices, content height, clamping).
- `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/RigDebugPanelLayoutTests.cs` (new) — EditMode coverage of the layout math.
Out of scope: rig drawing, focus/selection behavior, DNA, runtime code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The panel header toggles collapsed/expanded; collapsed height equals the header height only.
- The panel can be dragged by its header and resized by a bottom-right grip; both persist across SceneView repaints and editor restarts.
- Panel position and size are clamped to the SceneView so the panel cannot be lost off-screen.
- The `Bone width` label occupies its own reserved row, and the button rows follow it; no row overlaps any other row for any overlay state.
- Expanded panel height always fits its content (no clipping/overdraw) unless the user resized it larger.
- Rig drawing, focus, click-selection, and labels behave exactly as before.

## Validation
- EditMode: new `RigDebugPanelLayoutTests` (row ordering, content height covers every row, collapse height, clamp range).
- Unity: full solution compiles, console clean, and a manual SceneView check of collapse/expand, drag, resize, and the bone-width row.
- Record the exact checks and results on this task.

## Findings
(empty)

## Blockers
(empty)

## Next Step
Implement the layout helper, rework `DrawOverlayControls`, add tests, then compile and validate in Unity.

## Implementation
`Assets/Scripts/Editor/RigDebugView.cs`:
- Replaced the fixed `GUILayout.BeginArea(new Rect(10,10,290,280), "Rig Debug", GUI.skin.window)` with a self-managed panel rect.
- Header hosts an `EditorGUI.Foldout`: the panel collapses to the 20px header and expands again; collapsed state persists in `EditorPrefs`.
- Panel drags by the header and resizes by a bottom-right grip (diagonal `MouseCursor.ResizeUpLeft`). Position/size persist in `EditorPrefs` and are clamped to the SceneView. Body clicks are swallowed so they do not clear the bone selection.
- Body now uses explicit per-row rects. `Bone width` owns `Row.LineWidthLabel` between the slider and the button rows, and panel height is computed from the row count, so the controls after it are pushed down and cannot overlap the label.
- `EditorGUI.Toggle`/`Foldout`/`LabelField` take explicit `GUIContent` labels.

New: `Assets/Scripts/Editor/RigDebugPanelLayout.cs` (pure layout math) and `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/RigDebugPanelLayoutTests.cs`.

## Validation
- Unity 6000.5.9f1, MCP bridge port 6401; `refresh_unity(compile=request, scope=all, wait_for_ready=true)`.
- `ProceduralCreature.Editor.dll` rebuilt 2026-09-12 23:37; `read_console(error|warning)` = 0 entries.
- EditMode focused: `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor.RigDebugPanelLayoutTests` -> 11/11 passed.
- EditMode full suite -> 184/184 passed (3.21s).
- Evidence the enabled body actually draws: the first successful compile emitted 5 `Unable to find style '<label>' in skin 'DarkSkin'` warnings (Layout + Repaint); those come only from the new body path. They disappeared after the `GUIContent` fix.

## Residual risk / manual gate
- Collapse click, header drag, and grip resize are real SceneView mouse interactions. MCP cannot inject SceneView input or capture the SceneView in this session, so these remain manual.
- `GUIUtility.hotControl` is the standard route for drag events inside `duringSceneGui`, but it is runtime-verified only to the extent that the panel draws with a clean console.
- The pure clamp/size/height math the interactions drive is covered by the new tests.

## Fix: collapse toggle was a silent no-op (reported by user)
User report (verbatim): "It looks very nice and resize works (good job), but toggle doesn't. The title highlights onmouseover, but the toggle arrow does not and clicking on either does nothing. Enable rig overlay hides everything, which is alright and can be left in, but wasn't really what was asked for"

Root cause: `DrawPanelHeader` compared `EditorGUI.Foldout(...)` against the pre-call `expanded` local, then assigned `_collapsed = !expanded` using that OLD value. Because `expanded == !_collapsed`, the assignment reduced to `_collapsed = _collapsed` -- a silent no-op. The header therefore highlighted on hover but never collapsed or expanded.

Fix: capture the RETURNED value and map it through the now-tested pure helper `RigDebugPanelLayout.CollapsedFromFoldout(newExpanded)`, so the new collapsed state is derived from the returned expanded value. Drag, resize, and row layout are unchanged. The `Enable rig overlay` toggle is intentionally kept per the user's note.

## Validation (after fix)
- `refresh_unity` -> `ProceduralCreature.Editor.dll` rebuilt 2026-09-12 23:47; `read_console(error|warning)` = 0 entries.
- EditMode focused `RigDebugPanelLayoutTests`: 12/12 passed; added `CollapsedFromFoldout_IsTheInverseOfTheReportedExpandedState`.
- EditMode full suite: 185/185 passed (3.04s).
- Recovered a stale `tests_running` MCP job that survived the domain reload (persisted in SessionState) by invoking `MCPForUnity.Editor.Services.TestJobManager.ClearStuckJob()`; `clear_stuck` on `run_tests` did not reach the handler through `batch_execute`. Recorded in repo memory.

## Residual manual check
Clicking the header now derives collapse from the returned expanded value. Confirm in the SceneView that a header click collapses and expands the panel; drag, resize, and the width row were already confirmed by the user.
